docs.hands.component: A HAND THAT BELONGS TO A PERSON, not to a spot on the felt.
The areas on the live desk are places the DESK decided on: two boxes at two fixed points, and a
player is whoever happens to be nearest one. At a round table there is nothing to be near —
where somebody sits is read out of their own camera — so the hand is fastened to the AVATAR
instead, and it stands on whichever side of that person has felt left before the edge.
And it is the size of what is in it. Empty it is a mark saying only 'this is somebody's'; dealt
to, it grows; past the width the table can spare it stops growing and the cards close up
instead. A fixed box would be a permanent hole in the middle of the table for a player holding
nothing, which at a round desk is most players most of the time.
Everybody sees every hand, face and all. Hiding is a real thing and the kit does it, and it is a
second subject: with the cards hidden a reader watching one screen could not tell 'they did
nothing' from 'they did something I may not see'. What is here is the other half — who may reach
into a hand that is not theirs, and that is the owner's to decide.
docs.hands.scene: HANDS — two people at a round table, each with a patch of felt of their own.
Deal to yourself and to the other player: take a card off the deck in the middle and let it go
over either hand. It goes in, on both screens, and the patch grows to hold it — including the
patch that is not yours, because putting a card into somebody's hand is the ordinary thing a
player at a table does and this desk has no rule saying otherwise.
Drag your own disc and your hand travels with it, and it changes sides when the side it was on
runs out of table. Nothing decides that but the two points: a player at the top has felt below
them, and one at the right has felt to the left.
Then shut the hand — tap your own disc, or turn the knob for the bottom seat. It is washed in
its owner's colour, and from the other screen it stops answering: a card let go of over it is
not taken and comes back, and a card lying in it cannot be picked up at all, so the finger drives
the camera instead. From its OWN screen nothing has changed, because the lock is about everybody
NO SERVER. The two screens are two views of one tree, and the lock is a number on the zone rather
than a state in either screen — which is why the two cannot disagree about whether it is on.
